purpose: Signature-based partial validation of background rules R1-R3 (flow CSVs only).
assumptions: Flow-level evidence only: the packet-level release with MAC-level ground truth is not available; "attack-related" is a partial, heuristic ground truth derived without R1-R3.

Service ports are matched on either side of a flow because CICFlowMeter orients a flow by its first packet; the endpoint on the service-port side is the server (victim for BruteForce/Web, responder for DNS).

Attackers and victims (BruteForce, Web, DNS) are derived only from signature flows with both endpoints in 192.168.137.0/24 or 205.174.165.0/24, following the dataset statement that malicious IoT devices attack IoT devices. R1 is therefore not tested independently for these captures; signature_raw reports how the rules treat all signature flows, including those with an Internet endpoint.

Attackers = smallest set of client-side addresses covering >= 80% of the testbed signature flows; victims = smallest set of server-side addresses covering >= 80% of the attackers' signature flows (at most 10 addresses each).

Every flow between an attacker and a victim (any port or protocol) is attack-related in the main definition (attacker_victim); it may include background between the same two devices, so the narrower "signature" definition is reported as well.

DNS Spoofing: a rogue responder is a testbed address other than the gateway 192.168.137.1 on the port-53 side of >= 5 UDP flows in which it sends packets (Total Bwd packets > 0 when it is the destination; as the source it sent the first packet), i.e. it answers DNS queries. Spoofed replies that carry the IP address of the real resolver (gateway or Internet) cannot be separated at flow level and are not captured. Flow-direction flips can produce such flows in normal traffic; the same heuristic applied to the Benign captures is reported as a false-positive baseline.

ARP Spoofing: 8.6.0.1 / 8.0.6.4 are ARP header bytes read as IPv4 addresses (0x0806 0x0001 / 0x0800 0x06 0x04). All ARP frames of a flow-timeout window (normal and spoofed) share one pseudo-flow, which also occurs in Benign, so the attacker cannot be read from it. The spoofing host is taken as the testbed host (not the gateway) with the largest protocol-0 (ICMP) fan-out to other testbed hosts (ICMP redirects of a forwarding man-in-the-middle host), accepted if the fan-out is >= 3 and >= 2x the runner-up; all its flows are then attack-related.
Flows not linked to an identified attacker are unconfirmed, not proven background: kept_attack_share and flagged_attack_share are lower bounds of the true attack shares.
Rates are computed on the raw flows of each capture (before the de-duplication and DOS/DDOS caps of flagged_loader.py), so they can differ slightly from the flag rates in flagged_data.parquet.
Flow Duration is in microseconds (CICFlowMeter); packets = Total Fwd Packet + Total Bwd packets.
